---
title: Data Collection & Cleaning
---

This project constructs its retrieval corpus from long-form travel blog content, with an emphasis on destination-centric narratives rather than short reviews or structured listings. The pipeline performs collection, cleaning, feature extraction, and geospatial enrichment before persisting records into a cloud-hosted relational database for downstream retrieval and modeling.

---

## Data Sources

The primary data source is public WordPress-hosted travel blogs, discovered via SerpAPI-powered Google searches (e.g. `travel site:wordpress.com`). This surfaces organically authored, destination-focused travel writing rather than curated travel platforms.

---

## Blog Discovery & Page Enumeration

Each result returned by SerpAPI is treated as a candidate blog domain. For each domain, the pipeline looks for a WordPress sitemap at common paths (`/post-sitemap.xml`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/sitemap-1.xml`, `/sitemap_index.xml`). If found, all listed URLs are extracted and filtered to drop pagination, category/tag/author pages, feeds, admin paths, and non-HTML media—leaving only individual post URLs. This sitemap-first strategy enables efficient, respectful crawling without brute-force URL guessing.

---

## Content Scraping

Each candidate post is fetched with `requests` and parsed with `BeautifulSoup` to extract:

- Page title, meta description, and author (when available)
- Main body text (paragraph-level content)

---

## Text Cleaning & Normalization

Raw content is normalized before storage: Unicode and quote/dash standardization, punctuation and symbol removal, lowercasing, whitespace collapsing, and replacement of symbols (e.g., `& → and`). This produces a clean text field used for both BM25 indexing and embedding generation.

---

## Feature Engineering

### Named Entity Recognition (NER)

spaCy NER is applied to each post's title and description to extract a plausible geopolitical or location entity (`GPE`, `LOC`), preferring multi-word place names and combining consecutive location entities where possible. This produces a structured `location_name` field.

### Geocoding

Extracted location names are geocoded to latitude/longitude via **ArcGIS** (through `geopy`), with a short delay between requests. Locations that fail to resolve are logged and skipped rather than blocking ingestion.

---

## URL & Content Filtering

Pagination, feeds, tag/category pages, and non-HTML resources are excluded up front. Records with no resolvable location are not persisted, and duplicate `page_url` values are rejected at the database level.

---

## Database Persistence

Cleaned and enriched records are written to an AWS RDS PostgreSQL database via SQLAlchemy. Each record includes:

- Blog domain and page URL
- Page title, description, and author
- Extracted destination name
- Latitude and longitude
- Fully cleaned textual content

The schema enforces uniqueness on `page_url`, and duplicate inserts are caught and skipped.

---

## Embeddings for Semantic Search

ModernBERT embeddings for the cleaned corpus are computed offline and uploaded to an AWS S3 bucket, separate from the RDS metadata store. The API loads these embeddings from S3 at startup to build the FAISS index used for semantic search (see [Methods](methods.qmd)).
